name: Wallfahrtskirche Kalvarienberg
kurzbeschreibung: The baroque pilgrimage church Wallfahrtskirche Kalvarienberg in Imst offers a contemplative Stations of the Cross, magnificent frescoes, and wide panoramic views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The baroque Wallfahrtskirche Kalvarienberg rises picturesquely on a wooded hill at around 890 metres above sea level above the traditional district capital of Imst in the Tiroler Oberland. Together with the historic Stations of the Cross and the passion chapels, this sacred monument forms an important spiritual ensemble and a popular local recreation destination. From the viewing terrace in front of the church portal, visitors enjoy an impressive panoramic view over the Imst basin, the Gurgl and Inn valleys, and the rugged rock formations of the Lechtaler Alpen and the Muttekopfgruppe.

History & Architecture

The origins of this place of worship date back to 1684, when dedicated citizens and clergy of Imst erected a first crucifixion group on the rocky knoll to deepen devotion to the Passion. Between 1709 and 1714, today's widely visible Kalvarienbergkirche was built under master builder Christian Zangerl. In 1779, the church was comprehensively redesigned and expanded according to plans by the Imst baroque master builder Franz Franziskus Penz. The architectural appearance of the hall church is characterized by a prominent ridge turret with a curved dome and a polygonally enclosed choir. Inside, the building delights with vivid, late baroque ceiling frescoes vividly illustrating scenes from the Passion of Christ, as well as a magnificent high altar with life-sized passion figures. Along the steeply ascending pilgrimage trail, 14 artistically crafted Stations of the Cross with faithfully restored reliefs line the path up to the Kalvarienberg.

Visit & Getting There

The Wallfahrtskirche Kalvarienberg is open during the day all year round and is freely accessible free of charge (usually open from 08:00 to 19:00). May devotions, Lenten Stations of the Cross processions, and contemplative church services are held here regularly. Arrival by public transport: Take ÖBB trains to Imst-Pitztal railway station, from there take VVT city buses to the town centre of Imst (bus stop Imst Stadtplatz or Rathausstraße). From the town centre, the signposted Kalvarienbergweg leads up to the pilgrimage church in an approx. 20-minute walk. By car: Via the Inntal motorway A12 to the Imst exit or via the Fernpass road B189 to the town centre; parking is available in the town centre or at the car park near the mountain railways/sports centre.

Tips

The climb along the historic Stations of the Cross leads along partly uneven paved and gravel paths as well as steps; sturdy footwear is recommended. For visitors with mobility impairments, limited access is available via the rear access road close to the churchyard. Combine your visit with a hike through the nearby wild Rosengartenschlucht gorge or take a stroll through the historic Weberviertel of Imst.
